implementation_notes: Realize the layer as one ordered chain of `std::function<bool(const Request&)>` rules (or a small Validator interface) executed by a single `accept()` before the handler; lambdas capture rule parameters, and a false return short-circuits the chain so rejected requests never reach application code. The chain replaces the classic interceptor class hierarchy, and when a server framework already offers a middleware hook, use that hook as the single wrapper instead so the chain cannot be bypassed. Prefer stateless validators over capturing std::function objects on hot paths to avoid per-request allocation.
pitfalls: std::function may allocate for large captures; on the hot path use small stateless lambdas, function_ref-like views, or a table of plain function pointers.

A validator must not outlive the request data it references, and must not capture references to temporaries; keep validators pure functions of the request, and validate before any async continuation takes ownership.
Throwing from a validator in a noexcept path or from a destructor terminates the process; decide reject-versus-throw once and keep it uniform.
